title: Major Literary Prizes (Post45 Data Collective)
author_or_editor: Claire Grossman, Juliana Spahr and Stephanie Young
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed dataset of US literary prize winners and judges (1918-2020) with Wikidata, VIAF and LCCN author identifiers; used for author discovery and prize-year verification.

title: Selected British Literary Prizes, 1990-2022 (Post45 Data Collective)
author_or_editor: Katherine Binhammer, Kanika Batra, Theo Gray and Maryse Jayasuriya
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed dataset of winners and shortlists of major British prizes (Booker, Whitbread, Orange, T. S. Eliot, James Tait Black and others) with book titles and VIAF identifiers; 1990-2000 rows used.

title: NYT Hardcover Fiction Bestsellers, 1931-2020 (Post45 Data Collective)
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed bestseller metadata with OCLC numbers and author authority identifiers; used for popular and commercial fiction discovery.

title: NEA Creative Writing Fellowships (Post45 Data Collective)
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed list of National Endowment for the Arts literature fellows from 1967; used to discover minor and mid-career US writers. A fellowship is evidence of activity, not of a particular book.

title: Asian American Literary Canon (Post45 Data Collective)
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed dataset of Asian American texts and authors ranked by instances of scholarly study, with publication years, genres and publishers.

title: Feminist Bookstore News, 1976-2000 (Post45 Data Collective)
author_or_editor: Julie R. Enszer, Salome Grasland, Cassidy Hunt and Michaela Hayes
reliability_notes: Archival article metadata from Feminist Bookstore News; used to discover feminist and lesbian small-press writers.

title: Ralph Ellison (Wikipedia)
reliability_notes: Article revision of October 2026; dates, bibliography with first-edition ISBNs and posthumous-publication history checked against Encyclopedia.com and the New World Encyclopedia.

title: Ralph Ellison (Encyclopedia.com, compiling Gale's Contemporary Authors and Contemporary Black Biography)
reliability_notes: Reproduces Gale reference entries; gives the older birth year 1914 and dates Flying Home 1997, both recorded as discrepancies.

title: Ralph Ellison (New World Encyclopedia)
reliability_notes: Independent corroboration of dates (1913-1994), the National Book Award (1953) and the 1965 Book Week poll.

title: List of winners and nominated authors of the Booker Prize (Wikipedia)
reliability_notes: Winners and shortlists 1969-2000 and the 1970 Lost Booker shortlist and longlist (awarded 2010), transcribed from the article's raw wikitext into research/installment_10/lists/booker_prize_1969_2000.csv (205 rows, 140 authors). The article cites the Booker Prize Foundation's own records (thebookerprizes.com) and Moseley, Booker Prize Novels 1969-2005 (DLB 326). Judges were not transcribed.

title: Philip Larkin (Wikipedia, via Wikiwand)
reliability_notes: Dates, appointments, publication history of The Less Deceived (Marvell Press 1955, 29 poems, eight from the late 1940s) and the 2003 Collected Poems arrangement; cross-checked against EBSCO, the New World Encyclopedia and the Sogang page.

title: Philip Larkin (EBSCO Research Starters)
reliability_notes: XX Poems (100 copies, insufficient postage), The Less Deceived (working title Various Poems; three reprintings in nine months after The Times review), High Windows sales; dates Required Writing 1984 (probably the US edition).

title: Philip Larkin (New World Encyclopedia)
reliability_notes: Gives XX Poems as 1953 (other sources 1951) and is the only source consulted that lists The Fantasy Poets No. 21 (1954); characterises the Oxford Book of Twentieth-Century English Verse as controversial and the All What Jazz introduction as polemical; dates Aubade 1977.

title: Without Metaphysics: The Poetry of Philip Larkin (Sogang University academic page)
reliability_notes: Academic essay with a chronology and bibliography: Jill (Fortune Press 1946), A Girl in Winter (Faber 1947), XX Poems (1951), Required Writing (1983), Collected Poems (Marvell/Faber 1988), the text and date (12 February 1967) of High Windows, and the view that critics took Larkin seriously only after High Windows. Authorship attributed from the site's host; not independently confirmed.

title: All What Jazz, first edition (Jonkers Rare Books catalogue record)
reliability_notes: Describes a copy of the Faber 1970 first edition of All What Jazz: A Record Diary 1961-68; AbeBooks listings agree (ISBN 0571092403). Trade description, not a library catalogue.

title: Aubade (The Philip Larkin Society, philiplarkin.com)
reliability_notes: Gives the completion date (29 November 1977) and first publication in The Times Literary Supplement, 23 December 1977.

title: Critical opinions (1): Larkin and the difficult subject (Gale Literature Resource Center)
reliability_notes: Independent corroboration that Aubade was begun in 1974, finished in 1977 and first printed in the TLS Christmas issue of 23 December 1977, and was Larkin's last substantial lyric.

title: Lorraine Hansberry (Encyclopaedia Britannica)
reliability_notes: Dates, the Woodlawn basis of A Raisin in the Sun, the New York Drama Critics' Circle Award, the 1961 film's Cannes award, marriage to Robert Nemiroff (1953-64); dates the book of To Be Young, Gifted and Black 1970 and calls the 1969 production a Broadway one, both recorded as discrepancies.

title: Lorraine Hansberry (Encyclopedia.com, compiling Gale's Contemporary Black Biography)
reliability_notes: Freedom (1951-53), the Montevideo peace congress (1952), the 1959 award over plays by O'Neill, Williams and MacLeish, Les Blancs at the Longacre (1970), the Random House 1965 Sidney Brustein, and Baldwin's 1969 introduction.

title: Hansberry, Lorraine: Introduction (Encyclopedia.com, Gale literary criticism entry)
reliability_notes: Critical introduction and principal works: 530 performances of Raisin, its ranking among American classics, the later charge of assimilationism, the 1984 expanded edition, 101 performances of Sidney Brustein, and descriptions of The Drinking Gourd and What Use Are Flowers?; lists the New American Library 1961 edition of Raisin.

title: Lorraine Hansberry (AmericanLiterature.com)
reliability_notes: Used only for her anonymous letters to The Ladder in the late 1950s, the 1963 cancer diagnosis and the description of The Movement (1964); no other source consulted covers these points, so they are treated as provisional.

title: Lorraine Hansberry Biography (Chicago Public Library)
reliability_notes: Corroborates 101 performances and the 12 January 1965 closing of Sidney Brustein, her work on Freedom, and the May 1964 speech that gave To Be Young, Gifted and Black its title.

title: Les blancs: the collected last plays of Lorraine Hansberry (Internet Archive catalogue record)
author_or_editor: Internet Archive (catalogue data from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)
reliability_notes: Catalogue record of the first edition (New York: Random House, 1972; ISBN 039446480X) containing Les Blancs, The Drinking Gourd and What Use Are Flowers?; notes a later edition of 1983.

title: Hansberry, Lorraine 1930-1965 (Encyclopedia.com, Gale entry with Leonard R. N. Ashley's 1990 essay)
author_or_editor: Gale / Cengage (compiled); essay by Leonard R. N. Ashley
reliability_notes: Ashley's essay, citing the Dictionary of Literary Biography vol. 7, documents Dore Schary's commission of The Drinking Gourd and describes What Use Are Flowers? as a short television play about the aftermath of nuclear war; principal works list Les Blancs 1970 and The Collected Last Plays 1972.

title: Albert L. Murray (Encyclopedia.com, compiling Gale's Contemporary Black Biography)
reliability_notes: Biography (Tuskegee 1939, NYU MA 1948, Sorbonne 1950, Air Force retirement 1962, Barnard 1981-83) and bibliography, including the 1983 Vintage retitling of The Omni-Americans.

title: Murray, Albert 1916- (Encyclopedia.com, compiling Gale's Contemporary Literary Criticism)
reliability_notes: Critical overview and principal works, including descriptions of The Omni-Americans, South to a Very Old Place (dated 1972), The Hero and the Blues, the Scooter novels (The Seven League Boots: Scooter as a touring bassist) and The Blue Devils of Nada; lists Reflections on Logic, Politics, and Reality (Braimanna, 1989), whose attribution is treated as unresolved.

title: Murray, Albert (Alabama Authors database)
reliability_notes: Birth at Nokomis and upbringing near Mobile; bibliography with publishers and dates, including Reflections on Logic, Politics, and Reality (1989). The database's institutional sponsor has not been confirmed.

title: Albert Murray (LibraryThing author page)
reliability_notes: Used to corroborate dates (Magazine Point upbringing; South to a Very Old Place 1971); gives the ASCAP-Deems Taylor Award as 1977, recorded as a discrepancy.

title: Albert Murray obituary (The Guardian, 23 August 2013)
reliability_notes: Dates (12 May 1916 - 18 August 2013), adoption, meeting Ellison at Tuskegee, wartime service and 1962 retirement, The Omni-Americans' critique of Baldwin, the National Book Critics Circle lifetime achievement award (1996) and the Harper Lee Award (1998).

title: Albert Murray (EBSCO Research Starters)
reliability_notes: Influence on Stanley Crouch and Wynton Marsalis, co-founding of Jazz at Lincoln Center in the 1980s, The Omni-Americans' critique of anthropological 'fakelore', and later works outside the period (2001, 2005).
